cultural.vision_reason: This is a hand-tailored strip-woven cotton smock with ikat-patterned and checked strips, a widespread traditional garment form across Mande-speaking peoples of the West African savanna including the Dyula (in Ghana/Côte d'Ivoire/Burkina Faso), consistent with the claimed ethnicity and region.

physical.title: smock
physical.summary: Smock made from a single cloth folded in two, with a hole cut for the head opening, and the sides below the armpits sewn together. The original cloth is of seven strips of machine-made cotton, the strips being of three different patterns using white, blue and red thread. Four strips have a pattern alternating rectangles of white cotton with blue ikat; two have a check of blue in warp and weft; and the seventh (placed in the centre) a different blue ikat pattern alternating with white rectangles with a red stripe running down the middle of the entire strip. The neck opening is lined with a dark factory made  blue denim material.
